options: It can address specific compression needs with different characteristics
It allows for a single type of compression
It reduces the need for any compression
It eliminates the need for limiters
key: It can address specific compression needs with different characteristics

questions.stem: What is a potential danger of turning the attack control too high on a compressor?
options: It can make the sound flat and lifeless
It can add unwanted reverb
It can increase the volume too much
It can make the sound too dynamic
key: It can make the sound flat and lifeless

questions.stem: What is the main benefit of soft-knee compression?
options: It makes the onset of gain reduction less obvious.
It enhances the natural sound of instruments.
It increases the attack time.
It reduces the need for a compressor.
key: It makes the onset of gain reduction less obvious.

questions.stem: What is a potential side effect of using fast attack and release times?
options: Pumping and breathing effects.
No change in the signal.
Increased dynamic range.
Reduced signal clarity.
key: Pumping and breathing effects.

questions.stem: What is one common problem with percussive bass sounds like kick drums when using compressors?
options: They lose bass content if the attack time is under 50ms.
They maintain the original sound balance.
They increase the content of low frequencies.
They enhance the higher frequencies.
key: They lose bass content if the attack time is under 50ms.

questions.stem: What is a common application of parallel compression in audio processing?
options: To reduce underlying effects where fast attack and release times are necessary.
To enhance the sound of acoustic instruments.
To eliminate the need for compressors.
To increase the volume of high frequencies.
key: To reduce underlying effects where fast attack and release times are necessary.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of using an initial layer of gain reduction in vocal compression?
options: To even out overall levels
To increase the volume of the vocals
To add more reverb to the vocals
To distort the vocal sound
key: To even out overall levels

questions.stem: What is the key to fluent balancing according to the text?
options: Letting the faders set the agenda
Ignoring fader instability
Using as many plug-ins as possible
Rebuilding the plugin structure multiple times
key: Letting the faders set the agenda

questions.stem: What should be your first priority when balancing a mix?
options: Achieving a solid balance without artifacts
Using the loudest settings
Ensuring each instrument sounds stunning
Adding as many tracks as possible
key: Achieving a solid balance without artifacts

questions.stem: What is confirmation bias in the context of audio mixing?
options: The tendency to perceive things as we expect them to be.
The tendency to always trust new technology.
The tendency to perceive things as they actually are.
The tendency to ignore all biases.
key: The tendency to perceive things as we expect them to be.

questions.stem: What is one method suggested to combat confirmation bias in audio mixing?
options: Use a plug-in's bypass button and toggle it without looking.
Only rely on meters.
Avoid using any software tools.
Always trust your initial settings.
key: Use a plug-in's bypass button and toggle it without looking.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of using Lacinato's ABX/Shootouter software?
options: To reduce bias when comparing audio signals.
To enhance sound quality automatically.
To eliminate all audio processing errors.
To simplify the mixing process.
key: To reduce bias when comparing audio signals.

questions.stem: According to Fabian Marasciullo, what is a common practice when a mix setting does not work as desired?
options: Start over and try a different approach.
Ignore the issue and proceed.
Keep using the same settings.
Use the same processor repeatedly.
key: Start over and try a different approach.

questions.stem: What is a common challenge when mixing music with premixed elements such as loops or samples?
options: Adapting those samples at mixdown in order to fit them into their new arrangement context.
Balancing the volume levels
Finding the right tempo
Choosing the correct instruments
key: Adapting those samples at mixdown in order to fit them into their new arrangement context.

questions.stem: Why is low-pass filtering particularly useful in audio mixing?
options: It helps manage low-end phase problems
It adds more bass to the track
It increases the overall volume
It enhances high-frequency sounds
key: It helps manage low-end phase problems

questions.stem: According to the text, what is more important than the gear used in mixing?
options: The person using the gear
The brand of the gear
The price of the gear
The color of the gear
key: The person using the gear

questions.stem: What does the text suggest about low-budget processing?
options: It can still deliver a great mix.
It requires expensive plug-ins.
It is always inferior to high-budget processing.
It should be avoided at all costs.
key: It can still deliver a great mix.

questions.stem: What is one of the toughest mixing challenges mentioned in the text?
options: Rebalancing premixed audio
Finding a usable studio
Choosing a usable microphone
Selecting usable headphones
key: Rebalancing premixed audio

questions.stem: What does the text imply about processing experiments that don't work?
options: They provide valuable learning experiences.
They are a waste of time.
They should be avoided.
They should be repeated until successful.
key: They provide valuable learning experiences.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of adding "sweetening" effects to a music production?
options: To enhance the balance of raw tracks
To reduce the quality of the mix
To obscure important musical details
To make the music sound worse
key: To enhance the balance of raw tracks

questions.stem: According to Lee DeCarlo, what are effects compared to in music production?
options: Makeup and cosmetic surgery
Painting and drawing
Cooking and baking
Writing and editing
key: Makeup and cosmetic surgery

questions.stem: What does Russ Elevado say about using reverb in a mix?
options: He waits until halfway through the mix
He uses it at the beginning of the mix
He never uses reverb
He uses it excessively
key: He waits until halfway through the mix

questions.stem: What is the effect of reverb on the blend of individual tracks in a mix?
options: It pushes tracks away from the listener.
It decreases the depth of the mix.
It makes tracks sound more disconnected.
It brings tracks closer to the listener.
key: It pushes tracks away from the listener.

questions.stem: How does artificial reverb affect the size of a mix's acoustic environment?
options: It increases the apparent dimensions.
It decreases the apparent dimensions.
It makes tracks sound recorded in a smaller room.
It has no effect on the size.
key: It increases the apparent dimensions.

questions.stem: What role does reverb play in the sustain of a dry sound?
options: It increases the sustain.
It decreases the sustain.
It has no effect on sustain.
It makes sustain irrelevant.
key: It increases the sustain.

questions.stem: What is a challenge when using multiple reverb enhancements at once?
options: They can be difficult to adjust independently.
They are easy to adjust independently.
They can be applied without any issues.
They always improve the mix.
key: They can be difficult to adjust independently.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of a reverb plug-in control?
options: To adjust the balance of wet and dry signals
To increase the volume of the track
To change the pitch of the audio
To add distortion effects
key: To adjust the balance of wet and dry signals

questions.stem: What is a key advantage of digital convolution processors in reverb design?
options: They can recreate reverb with unparalleled realism
They are the earliest type of reverb
They use springs to create sound
They are not suitable for tonal enhancements
key: They can recreate reverb with unparalleled realism

questions.stem: What can help you visualize the kind of space you want the blended sounds to inhabit?
options: Closing your eyes
Using only default presets
Reading the manual
Increasing the reverb tail
key: Closing your eyes

questions.stem: Why is it important to check the effect in mono when using reverb?
options: To prevent nasty tonal changes
To ensure volume balance
To enhance dynamic characteristics
To prevent audience immersion
key: To prevent nasty tonal changes

questions.stem: What should you do to better hear the reverb decay?
options: Mute and un-mute the track
Use a different plug-in
Increase the volume
Adjust the frequency balance
key: Mute and un-mute the track

questions.stem: What is one reason you might want to use a second blend reverb with less pre-delay?
options: To reduce masking of the wet signal by the dry signal
To add more low frequencies
To increase the stereo spread
To enhance the brightness of the sound
key: To reduce masking of the wet signal by the dry signal

questions.stem: Name the main controls to worry about when using a delay plug-in.
options: Feedback, Time, Mix
Bass, Treble, Gain
Volume, Pitch, Reverb
Attack, Release, Threshold
key: Feedback, Time, Mix

questions.stem: What are the benefits of using delay effects over reverb in audio mixing?
options: Delay effects provide more control over timing and rhythm.
Delay effects are easier to use than reverb.
Delay effects create a more natural sound environment.
Delay effects are more suitable for live performances.
key: Delay effects provide more control over timing and rhythm.

questions.stem: Describe the difference between a send-return effect configuration and an insert setup when using delay effects.
options: A send-return configuration allows for parallel processing of the delay effect, while an insert setup processes the effect in series with the original signal.
Both configurations process the effect in series with the original signal.
A send-return configuration processes the effect in series with the original signal, while an insert setup allows for parallel processing of the delay effect.
Both configurations allow for parallel processing of the delay effect.
key: A send-return configuration allows for parallel processing of the delay effect, while an insert setup processes the effect in series with the original signal.

questions.stem: What is the advantage of making delays sonically different to the dry tracks?
options: It creates a more immersive sound experience.
It reduces the overall volume of the track.
It makes the track sound more monotonous.
It eliminates the need for any effects.
key: It creates a more immersive sound experience.

questions.stem: What is a common problem when using a single 50 to 100ms short 'slapback' delay with little or no feedback?
options: It creates a muddy sound
It results in a thin sound
It causes phase cancellation
It introduces unwanted distortion
key: It creates a muddy sound

questions.stem: The benefits of using tempo-synchronized delays in music production include:
options: Improved timing and rhythm consistency
Reduced sound quality
Increased distortion and noise
Faster tempo changes
key: Improved timing and rhythm consistency

questions.stem: The role of poly rhythmic delay in enhancing rhythmic energy in music is to:
options: create complex rhythmic patterns
reduce the tempo
simplify the rhythm
eliminate rhythmic variations
key: create complex rhythmic patterns

questions.stem: Delays are often preferred over reverbs for modern music styles because:
options: they create a sense of space without cluttering the mix.
they are more affordable.
they are easier to use.
they are more traditional.
key: they create a sense of space without cluttering the mix.

questions.stem: What are some of the benefits of using delay effects in audio mixing?
options: Enhances spatial perception and depth
Increases the need for reverb
Increases the tempo of the track
Destroys vocal clarity
key: Enhances spatial perception and depth

questions.stem: Which of the following is a tactic to enhance the stereo spread of any echo?
options: Use a single echo panned to the opposite side of the stereo panorama
Use only mono delays
Increase the volume of the dry signal
Avoid using delay effects
key: Use a single echo panned to the opposite side of the stereo panorama

questions.stem: The session runs at 120 BPM and your delay plugin has no tempo sync, so you have to type a time in milliseconds. What do you enter for a dotted eighth note delay?
options: 250 ms
375 ms
500 ms
750 ms
key: 375 ms

questions.stem: A straight eighth note delay on a busy vocal makes the line harder to follow, because every repeat lands on the next syllable. What does the module suggest trying before you give up on the delay?
options: More feedback, so the repeats blend together
A louder return, so the repeats read as intentional
A dotted eighth, which lands between the beats
A reverb, since delay does not suit dense vocals
key: A dotted eighth, which lands between the beats

questions.stem: You want one delay shared by the vocal, the acoustic guitar and the piano, with a different amount of it on each. How do you set that up?
options: A copy of the delay inserted on each of the three tracks
One delay on an aux return, fed by a separate send from each track
The delay inserted on the vocal, with the other two routed through it
The delay inserted on the master buss, with the wet mix pulled back
key: One delay on an aux return, fed by a separate send from each track

questions.stem: The delay return is already quieter than the vocal, but the repeats still pull your ear off the dry track. What does the module have you do to the return?
options: Raise the feedback so the repeats blur into each other
Boost the presence range on the return so it matches the vocal
Roll off the top and bottom of the return so the repeats sit behind
Pan the return hard to one side and leave the level alone
key: Roll off the top and bottom of the return so the repeats sit behind

questions.stem: You sum the master to mono after a widening move. Select every result that means the move is taking more than it gives.
options: The low end drops
The stereo image collapses toward the center
The widened source gets quieter or thinner
The widened part disappears almost entirely
key: The low end drops
The widened source gets quieter or thinner
The widened part disappears almost entirely

questions.stem: You add a delay to widen an acoustic guitar. Instead of reading as width it smears the guitar and blurs its attack. The return is panned to the same side as the dry track and the time is set to 120 ms. What do you change first?
options: Add feedback so the repeats fill in behind the guitar
Boost the top end of the return so the repeats cut through
Pan the return opposite the source and shorten the time to 15 to 30 ms
Raise the return level until the width becomes obvious
key: Pan the return opposite the source and shorten the time to 15 to 30 ms

questions.stem: Two ways to widen a pad: a stereo imager that inverts the polarity of the side content, or a 20 ms delay panned opposite the source. Which one holds together better when the mix is summed to mono?
options: The imager, because it works on level rather than phase
The delay, because an offset in time mostly survives summing
Both equally, since mono summing only removes the panning
Neither, so width is always a stereo only decision
key: The delay, because an offset in time mostly survives summing

questions.stem: A student duplicates one guitar take onto a second track, pans the two copies hard left and hard right, and raises both faders. The guitar gets louder but no wider. Why?
options: The two hard pans cancel each other at the master buss
A duplicated track is automatically out of polarity with its source
Width comes from difference between the channels, and the sides are identical
The pans are right but the delay between the two sides is wrong
key: Width comes from difference between the channels, and the sides are identical

questions.stem: How does the module tell you to find the level for a delay return?
options: Match the return level to the level of the dry track and leave it
Leave the plugin wet and dry mix control at its halfway default
Raise it until clearly audible, then lower it until you notice it only when it stops
Set it so the return meter has only just started to move
key: Raise it until clearly audible, then lower it until you notice it only when it stops

questions.stem: Why does the procedure guide have you match loudness before comparing the bypassed and active delay?
options: Bypassing the plugin resets the delay time back to its default value
Louder almost always wins, so an unmatched comparison proves only which is louder
Plugin latency makes the bypassed signal arrive ahead of the processed one
The output meters will not read the same until the two levels match
key: Louder almost always wins, so an unmatched comparison proves only which is louder

questions.stem: Your delay time is exactly on the grid, but against the drummer it sits stiff and fights the feel of the track. What does the module tell you to do?
options: Raise the feedback so the timing error gets buried in the repeats
Quantize the drums so that they agree with the delay timing
Switch to a reverb, since this tempo will not support a delay
Tap it against the track and keep a value slightly off the grid if it sits better
key: Tap it against the track and keep a value slightly off the grid if it sits better

questions.stem: Select every move that adds real width and still mostly survives a mono sum.
options: A stereo imager that inverts the polarity of the side content
A 15 to 30 ms delay panned opposite the source
Raising the fader on a track that is already panned hard left
Two separately performed takes panned left and right
key: A 15 to 30 ms delay panned opposite the source
Two separately performed takes panned left and right

questions.stem: Your delay sits on an aux return fed by a post fader send from the vocal. You pull the vocal fader down 3 dB for the verse. What happens to the repeats?
options: They stay where they were, so the delay becomes more prominent
They get louder, because more signal is left over for the aux
They drop with the fader, so the wet to dry ratio stays where you set it
Nothing changes until you reopen the send and reset its level
key: They drop with the fader, so the wet to dry ratio stays where you set it

questions.stem: Why is low frequency content the riskiest thing in a mix to widen?
options: Low frequencies cannot be panned in a DAW at all
Phase based width cancels in mono, and losing the lows costs the mix its weight
Low frequencies are omnidirectional, so widening them does nothing audible
Widening the lows always pushes the peak level into clipping
key: Phase based width cancels in mono, and losing the lows costs the mix its weight

questions.stem: The song has a tempo map and the bridge slows down. Your delay time was calculated for the verse tempo and typed into the plugin. What happens, and what is the fix?
options: Nothing happens, because millisecond values do not depend on tempo
The repeats get louder in the bridge, so pull the feedback down
The repeats drift off the beat in the bridge, so switch the plugin to tempo sync
The plugin doubles the time by itself, so halve the note value
key: The repeats drift off the beat in the bridge, so switch the plugin to tempo sync

questions.stem: What is a track created from pieces of multiple takes in order to create a better overall performance?
options: Comp track
Top to Tail
Patchwork
Take
key: Comp track

questions.stem: When recording a take, what would you call the style where the engineer records a take from the beginning of the song to the end?
options: Top to Tail
Comp track
Patchwork
key: Top to Tail

questions.stem: A technique that records a set of two or more tracks that have the same musical part, but different performances of that part is called:
options: Double Track
Comping
Top to Tail
Patchwork
key: Double Track

questions.stem: What does Tony Platt suggest about the mixing process?
options: It should be done after recording
It should begin the moment you start recording
It is the least important part of production
It should be outsourced to professionals
key: It should begin the moment you start recording

questions.stem: What is comping in the context of music production?
options: Recording a single take and using it as is
Recording multiple takes and editing the best parts together
Using pre-recorded loops
Mixing tracks without editing
key: Recording multiple takes and editing the best parts together

questions.stem: Why is comping particularly recommended for lead vocals?
options: Lead vocals are usually perfect in one take
Lead vocals benefit from the best possible performance
Lead vocals are less important than other parts
Lead vocals are easier to record
key: Lead vocals benefit from the best possible performance

questions.stem: What is one downside of recording numerous full "top to tail" takes?
options: It requires less concentration from the musician
It demands more concentration and endurance from the musician
It is quicker than other methods
It results in fewer expressive moments
key: It demands more concentration and endurance from the musician

questions.stem: What is a disadvantage of recording a single track one phrase at a time?
options: It maintains musical flow
It can feel disjointed emotionally
It is more efficient
It requires less editing
key: It can feel disjointed emotionally

questions.stem: What is the recommended approach for comping in small-studio environments?
options: Record numerous full takes
Record one phrase at a time
Record section-length takes and use punch-ins as needed
Avoid comping altogether
key: Record section-length takes and use punch-ins as needed

questions.stem: How many takes per section are recommended for a professional-grade lead-vocal comp?
options: One
Three
Five
Eight
key: Eight

questions.stem: Your lead vocal comp plays back with a small click or a doubled consonant at the start of most lines. What is the most likely cause?
options: The edits were placed on the word attacks instead of in the quiet just before them
The crossfades are longer than the phrases they join, so the takes overlap
The comp was built on a duplicate playlist instead of on the original take lane
The takes were auditioned in cycle playback instead of soloed one at a time
key: The edits were placed on the word attacks instead of in the quiet just before them

questions.stem: Select every habit the course gives for keeping a comp edit inaudible.
options: Trim the clip boundary at a quiet crossing rather than inside a sustained note
Put a short fade or crossfade on every edit point
Copy the chosen phrase into the comp playlist without changing its musical position
Listen across each edit in the full mix rather than soloed
Raise the level of each promoted phrase to match the loudest take
Nudge each promoted phrase slightly early so it leads the beat
key: Trim the clip boundary at a quiet crossing rather than inside a sustained note
Put a short fade or crossfade on every edit point
Copy the chosen phrase into the comp playlist without changing its musical position
Listen across each edit in the full mix rather than soloed

questions.stem: You are joining two takes in the middle of a sustained vowel rather than at a consonant. How should this crossfade compare with one you would use at a transient?
options: Longer, because sustained material hides a longer fade
Shorter, because a sustained note exposes any change in level
Identical, because fade length is a session setting you choose once
No fade at all, because there is no transient there to click
key: Longer, because sustained material hides a longer fade

questions.stem: You comp the snare track on its own and choose a different take for one bar than the overheads use. What do you hear?
options: The kit smears at that bar, because every drum mic hears every drum
Only the snare changes there, because the overhead tracks are untouched
The snare gets louder there, because the two takes sum together
The snare shifts to the far side of the stereo image for that bar
key: The kit smears at that bar, because every drum mic hears every drum

questions.stem: Select every step the course has you take before you start comping a drum kit.
options: Group the drum tracks so one cut lands on all of them at once
Choose New from the track Playlist selector so the original takes stay available
Hide the other instruments so only the tracks you are comping are visible
Plan each cut to land in a gap rather than on a hit
Comp the overheads first, then cut each close mic to match them by ear
Consolidate every drum track into one clip before opening the playlist lanes
key: Group the drum tracks so one cut lands on all of them at once
Choose New from the track Playlist selector so the original takes stay available
Hide the other instruments so only the tracks you are comping are visible
Plan each cut to land in a gap rather than on a hit

questions.stem: A student comps every breath out of a lead vocal. What does the course say this costs?
options: The vocal sounds inhuman and the phrases run together
The vocal sits further forward because the quiet gaps are gone
The de-esser has less work to do on the hard consonants
The phrasing becomes harder to read on the waveform
key: The vocal sounds inhuman and the phrases run together

questions.stem: Your comp is technically clean and every join is inaudible, and the performance still sounds flat and uninvolving. What is the first move?
options: Comp it again by ear, choosing on phrasing and pitch instead of on the waveform
Lengthen every crossfade so the joins breathe and the phrases flow together
Raise the level of the comp lane and listen through the pass again
Promote more of the takes so there is more material to choose from
key: Comp it again by ear, choosing on phrasing and pitch instead of on the waveform

questions.stem: You have worked through every take of a chorus line and none of them has the pitch and the energy the section needs. What is the professional move?
options: Re-record the line, because comping cannot build a performance nobody played
Comp it syllable by syllable across all the takes until something works
Take the closest one and repair the pitch with a tuning plug in
Copy the verse version of the same line into the chorus instead
key: Re-record the line, because comping cannot build a performance nobody played

questions.stem: Why does the course have you choose New from the track Playlist selector before you build a comp?
options: It keeps the original takes on their own lanes while you assemble the performance
It renders the comped clips so the track needs less processing power
It groups the track with the other tracks recorded in the same pass
It is required before a fade or crossfade can be drawn on that track
key: It keeps the original takes on their own lanes while you assemble the performance

questions.stem: You cannot decide between two takes of the same phrase. Which listening method does the course recommend?
options: Loop the phrase and cycle the lanes so you hear each take in context
Solo each take and compare the height of the two waveforms on screen
Choose the take with the lowest background noise and fix the phrasing later
Bounce both takes and compare them in a separate session the next day
key: Loop the phrase and cycle the lanes so you hear each take in context

questions.stem: You are moving the piano part out of two late verses and into two earlier ones. Select every step the assignment requires.
options: Make a grid accurate selection before you move anything
Move the complete musical section rather than a fragment of it
Confirm that every track is still aligned after the move
Choose an entry point where the heavier piano energy sounds earned
Leave a copy of the piano in the original verses as a safety
Trim the moved section shorter so it clears the vocal entry
key: Make a grid accurate selection before you move anything
Move the complete musical section rather than a fragment of it
Confirm that every track is still aligned after the move
Choose an entry point where the heavier piano energy sounds earned

questions.stem: The assignment has you thin the backing vocals at the start of one verse so the stack is full by the next verse. What is the arrangement reason for doing that?
options: It gives the section somewhere to build to, so the full stack lands harder
It lowers the track count, which leaves the mix more headroom to work with
It removes the need to tune the backing vocals in that earlier verse
It makes the remaining backing vocal parts easier to comp and edit
key: It gives the section somewhere to build to, so the full stack lands harder

questions.stem: You duplicate a guitar track and build a double part from another take. What tells you the double is working rather than just making the part louder?
options: The two parts sit tight together and their small differences widen the part
The duplicate plays the identical audio file, so nothing can smear
The duplicate is polarity inverted against the original part
The duplicate is panned to the same position as the original part
key: The two parts sit tight together and their small differences widen the part

questions.stem: Between two comped phrases the background noise steps up and then back down, though no click is audible at the join. What is happening, and what fixes it?
options: The takes carry different room tone, so move the join into a gap and lengthen the fade
The crossfade is too long and is dipping the noise floor, so shorten it
A gate is opening and closing on the vocal, so raise its threshold
The comp playlist is out of polarity with the source lane, so invert it
key: The takes carry different room tone, so move the join into a gap and lengthen the fade

questions.stem: You are checking a finished lead vocal comp before you submit it. Select every item that would cost you credit.
options: A phrase is missing because a promoted range did not cover the whole line
A word plays twice where two takes overlap at the join
An edit point has been left with no fade on it
The background noise jumps at one of the joins
A breath is audible just before the start of a line
The original takes are still sitting on their own playlist lanes
key: A phrase is missing because a promoted range did not cover the whole line
A word plays twice where two takes overlap at the join
An edit point has been left with no fade on it
The background noise jumps at one of the joins

Only in the Canvas mobile app

key: An effect that adds low frequency energy to a signal that is still musically related to the unprocessed sound

questions.stem: An effect that automatically detects drum hits and replaces them with a sampled recording effectively replacing the original recording.
options: Drum Trigger or sample trigger
Virtual instrument
Impact transducer
key: Drum Trigger or sample trigger

questions.stem: Clipping is always a bad thing.
options: True
False
key: False

questions.stem: Distortion is the addition or loss of information from the original signal.
options: True
False
key: True

questions.stem: You can add gain to a signal forever without any change to the quality of the original signal.
options: True
False
key: False

questions.stem: When adding harmonic distortion to a signal, be aware that you are adding extra harmonic information to the signal below the fundamental.
options: True
False
key: False

questions.stem: One way to make use of the added high frequency information in a distorted signal is to use an EQ after the distortion to funnel the added spectral energy into those areas where it's really needed.
options: True
False
key: True

questions.stem: You A/B a saturated bass against the dry signal and the saturated one sounds better. What must you check before trusting that?
options: That the master fader is at unity
That both are at matched loudness, because saturation raises perceived level
That the session sample rate has not changed
That the saturation plugin is in mono
key: That both are at matched loudness, because saturation raises perceived level

questions.stem: What is the audible difference between soft clipping and hard clipping?
options: Soft clipping is inaudible and hard clipping is audible
Soft clipping raises level and hard clipping lowers it
Soft clipping only affects low frequencies
Soft clipping rounds the peaks and adds mostly lower order harmonics, hard clipping squares them and adds harsh upper harmonics
key: Soft clipping rounds the peaks and adds mostly lower order harmonics, hard clipping squares them and adds harsh upper harmonics

questions.stem: You want a bass to read on small speakers that cannot reproduce its fundamental. What does saturation give you?
options: Harmonics above the fundamental that imply the pitch the speaker cannot produce
A boost to the fundamental itself
A reduction in the dynamic range of the part
A wider stereo image for the bass
key: Harmonics above the fundamental that imply the pitch the speaker cannot produce

questions.stem: What distinguishes even order harmonics from odd order harmonics in how they sound?
options: Even order tends to sound warm and musical, odd order tends to sound aggressive or harsh
Even order is always inaudible, odd order is always audible
Even order raises level, odd order lowers it
Even order affects only the top octave
key: Even order tends to sound warm and musical, odd order tends to sound aggressive or harsh

questions.stem: A drum buss sounds lifeless after heavy compression. Why might light saturation help more than more compression?
options: It lowers the noise floor of the buss
It widens the stereo image of the drums
It adds harmonic content and apparent loudness without further reducing dynamics
It restores the transients that compression removed
key: It adds harmonic content and apparent loudness without further reducing dynamics

questions.stem: What is the most common mistake when using a distortion plugin on a full mix?
options: Setting the output level too low
Driving it hard enough that the low end loses definition and the top becomes harsh
Placing it before the master fader
Using it in mono rather than stereo
key: Driving it hard enough that the low end loses definition and the top becomes harsh

questions.stem: Why does parallel distortion often work better than inserting distortion directly?
options: Parallel routing avoids phase problems entirely
Parallel routing increases the sample rate
The dry signal keeps its transients and dynamics while the distorted signal adds weight
Parallel routing uses less CPU
key: The dry signal keeps its transients and dynamics while the distorted signal adds weight

questions.stem: Input drive and output level are set independently. Why does that matter when you judge the result?
options: Drive and output do the same thing at different resolutions
Output drive introduces latency and input drive does not
Only output level affects the harmonic content
Drive changes the character, output only changes level, and louder always sounds better
key: Drive changes the character, output only changes level, and louder always sounds better

questions.stem: What does tape saturation do to transients that clean gain does not?
options: It softens and rounds them, reducing peak level while keeping apparent loudness
It sharpens them and increases peak level
It leaves them unchanged and only adds noise
It delays them relative to the rest of the signal
key: It softens and rounds them, reducing peak level while keeping apparent loudness

questions.stem: Where in the chain would you place distortion intended to add weight to a bass part?
options: Before any EQ so the distortion shapes the raw signal
After the master fader for the whole mix
On the reverb return only
After corrective EQ so you are distorting the tone you actually want
key: After corrective EQ so you are distorting the tone you actually want

questions.stem: A distorted guitar sounds fine alone and disappears in the mix. What is a likely cause?
options: The distortion filled the midrange with harmonics that other parts are masking
The distortion removed the guitar's fundamental entirely
The guitar is out of polarity with itself
The distortion lowered its overall level
key: The distortion filled the midrange with harmonics that other parts are masking

questions.stem: Why does distortion make a source seem louder even when the meter reading has not changed?
options: Distortion shifts the source forward in the stereo field
Distortion lowers the noise floor so more detail is audible
Added harmonics increase perceived loudness without raising peak level
Distortion raises the peak level but not the meter reading
key: Added harmonics increase perceived loudness without raising peak level

questions.stem: What should you listen for to know distortion has gone too far on a vocal?
options: The vocal moving to one side of the stereo image
The vocal level dropping below the instruments
The reverb tail shortening
Sibilance turning harsh and the consonants becoming brittle
key: Sibilance turning harsh and the consonants becoming brittle

questions.stem: Why is it worth checking a distorted part against the dry signal at matched loudness?
options: Matching loudness removes the harmonic content
It is the only way to check for phase problems
Matched loudness is required by the bounce specification
Distortion raises perceived loudness, and louder is not the same as better
key: Distortion raises perceived loudness, and louder is not the same as better

questions.stem: What is clip gain used for that a distortion plugin is not?
options: Adding harmonic content to a dull source
Softening transients on a drum buss
Widening the stereo image
Correcting level before the signal reaches any processing
key: Correcting level before the signal reaches any processing

questions.stem: Heavily distorting the low end of a mix causes what specific problem?
options: The low end moves to the right of the stereo field
The low end drops below the noise floor
Harmonics in the low mids muddy the mix and the bass loses definition
The bass shifts out of polarity with the kick
key: Harmonics in the low mids muddy the mix and the bass loses definition

questions.stem: You need a source to cut through without raising its level. Which is the better first move and why?
options: A wide low shelf boost, because it adds weight
A longer reverb, because it adds size
Hard limiting, because it raises the average level
Light saturation, because the added harmonics sit where small speakers and ears are most sensitive
key: Light saturation, because the added harmonics sit where small speakers and ears are most sensitive

questions.stem: Why is it recommended to tighten the timing of each layer one at a time?
options: To save time by editing all layers together
To ensure each layer fits the groove in isolation
To avoid phase incoherence
To make the process more challenging
key: To ensure each layer fits the groove in isolation

questions.stem: What is a common issue with small-studio band recordings according to the text?
options: Overly complex arrangements
Inconsistent timing due to a talentless drummer
Excessive use of MIDI files
Lack of creative input
key: Inconsistent timing due to a talentless drummer

questions.stem: What is a potential downside of quantizing a drummer's performance?
options: It makes the performance sound too human
It can make the performance sound unmusical
It simplifies the mixing process
It enhances the drummer's natural rhythm
key: It can make the performance sound unmusical

questions.stem: What should be done when live elements are mixed with machine elements?
options: Ensure everything is very synced up
Ignore timing discrepancies
Focus only on the live elements
Use only machine elements for consistency
key: Ensure everything is very synced up

questions.stem: What is a common oversight in timing correction for small-studio engineers?
options: Ignoring the timing of rhythm guitars
Over-editing the drum parts
Neglecting the timing of lead vocals
Focusing too much on bass timing
key: Neglecting the timing of lead vocals

questions.stem: What can the waveform profile of the reference instrument provide during editing?
options: A visual template for editing other layers
A distraction from the main task
A guide for mixing levels
An unnecessary complication
key: A visual template for editing other layers

questions.stem: What is a common reason why small-studio operators may not perform all necessary timing adjustments?
options: Lack of appropriate software
Insufficient audio-editing skills
High cost of editing tools
Limited access to audio files
key: Insufficient audio-editing skills

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a crossfade in audio editing?
options: To increase the volume of the audio
To avoid audible clicks at edit points
To add effects to the audio
To change the pitch of the audio
key: To avoid audible clicks at edit points

questions.stem: Where is the easiest place to hide edit points in audio?
options: In the middle of a sustained note
In gaps in the audio
At the start of a track
During a loud chorus
key: In gaps in the audio

questions.stem: What is backward temporal masking in audio editing?
options: A technique to increase audio volume
A method to reduce noise
A psychological effect where a later event conceals an earlier one
A way to change the pitch of audio
key: A psychological effect where a later event conceals an earlier one

questions.stem: You enable Elastic Audio on the drum tracks, leave the algorithm set to Polyphonic, and after the timing pass the kit flams and the hits sound smeared. What is the fix?
options: Switch the drum tracks to Rhythmic and run the timing pass again
Drop the quantize strength by half and run the timing pass again
Shorten the crossfades at each of the warp markers you moved
Turn Elastic Audio off and nudge every drum clip into place by hand
key: Switch the drum tracks to Rhythmic and run the timing pass again

questions.stem: Select every Elastic Audio pairing the course teaches.
options: Rhythmic on the drum tracks
Monophonic on a single note line such as a bass
Polyphonic on a track carrying chords
Elastique Pro on most of the non drum tracks in the Timing Lab
Varispeed on a lead vocal whose pitch must not change
Rhythmic on sustained pads so that they stay smooth
key: Rhythmic on the drum tracks
Monophonic on a single note line such as a bass
Polyphonic on a track carrying chords
Elastique Pro on most of the non drum tracks in the Timing Lab

questions.stem: You quantize a drum performance at 100 percent strength and the groove dies. What does the course tell you to do instead?
options: Use a partial strength, around 50 to 70 percent, so the hits move toward the grid
Quantize at full strength, then shift the whole track slightly late
Quantize at full strength and restore the feel with reverb
Leave the timing alone and let the click track cover the drift
key: Use a partial strength, around 50 to 70 percent, so the hits move toward the grid

questions.stem: You drag a warp marker to pull one late hit onto the beat and the entire clip slides with it. What did you skip?
options: Setting a warp marker on each side of the one you moved, to anchor the rest
Switching the track view to Warp before you started editing
Changing the track from samples to ticks before you started
Letting Pro Tools finish analyzing the track after you enabled it
key: Setting a warp marker on each side of the one you moved, to anchor the rest

questions.stem: Everything between two warp markers stretches to pay for a move. What does that mean for how you work?
options: Small moves with close anchors do the least damage to the audio
The stretch spreads across the whole track, so marker placement does not matter
Only the audio after the marker stretches, so anchor ahead of the move only
The stretch is lossless, so the distance you move a transient has no cost
key: Small moves with close anchors do the least damage to the audio

questions.stem: A bass part felt good, you pulled it onto the grid, and now the track feels stiff and you cannot say why. What should you have done before editing?
options: Listened to the part against the kick, because pushing or dragging on purpose is not an error
Compared the part against the grid on screen and trusted what the waveform showed
Quantized the kick to match the bass rather than the other way round
Added swing to the grid first and then quantized the bass to it
key: Listened to the part against the kick, because pushing or dragging on purpose is not an error

questions.stem: The Timing Lab has you change every track from samples to ticks and confirm the icon has turned into a metronome. What does that setting do?
options: It ties the clips to the tempo map so they follow tempo changes
It switches the timeline ruler over to bars and beats
It locks the clips in place so that an edit cannot move them
It converts the audio files to a higher sample rate for stretching
key: It ties the clips to the tempo map so they follow tempo changes

questions.stem: You are tightening a doubled vocal against the lead. Which points have to line up for the double to do its job?
options: The consonants, the breaths and the note changes
The peak level of every word in the phrase
The vibrato rate on the sustained notes
The start and the end of each clip
key: The consonants, the breaths and the note changes

questions.stem: You set a fast correction speed on a lead vocal and the front of every note now sounds clipped and mechanical. What has the fast setting taken away?
options: The scoop up into the note, which was part of the performance
The consonant at the start of the word
The vibrato on the tail of the note
The formant, so the singer sounds like a different person
key: The scoop up into the note, which was part of the performance

questions.stem: You move a note up several semitones and the singer suddenly sounds smaller and younger. Which control do you reach for?
options: Formant preservation
Correction speed
Note transition
Scale and key
key: Formant preservation

questions.stem: A vocal is being tuned with the key and scale set wrong for the section. What do you hear?
options: Notes dragged onto pitches the song does not use, so the tool fights the singer
The whole vocal shifted up or down by one fixed interval
Nothing, because the key setting only changes what the editor displays
A loss of high end on every note the tool corrects
key: Notes dragged onto pitches the song does not use, so the tool fights the singer

questions.stem: Select every part of a vocal the Mix Tuning Assignment tells you not to over correct.
options: Consonants
Breaths
Scoops into notes
Expressive transitions between notes
A sustained note that sits flat for its whole length
A background vocal sitting out of tune with the lead
key: Consonants
Breaths
Scoops into notes
Expressive transitions between notes

questions.stem: Melodyne runs inside Pro Tools through ARA. What does that change about getting audio into it?
options: It reads the clip on the track directly, with no transfer pass and no ReWire to set up
It needs an Aux Input carrying a ReWire plug in before it can see the track
It analyzes only while the song plays, so the part has to be scanned in real time
It analyzes only after the track has been bounced and reimported
key: It reads the clip on the track directly, with no transfer pass and no ReWire to set up

questions.stem: The standard Pro Tools undo command will reverse a pitch edit you made inside Melodyne.
options: True
False
key: False

questions.stem: You tune a background vocal stack until every note sits dead center, and the stack now sounds thinner and smaller than it did before. Why?
options: The small pitch differences between the layers were what gave the stack its width
Correcting pitch lowers the level of every layer in the stack
The layers should have been tuned to each other rather than to the lead
Formant preservation was left switched on across the whole stack
key: The small pitch differences between the layers were what gave the stack its width

questions.stem: What is an EQ? (mark all that apply)
options: A frequency-specific volume knob.
A device that lets you control the dynamic range of a signal
A device that uses changes in phase to change the volume of specific frequencies
key: A frequency-specific volume knob.
A device that uses changes in phase to change the volume of specific frequencies

questions.stem: When the sound of cymbals block your perception of the vocals above 5 kHz, it is called
options: Frequency Masking
Cymbology
Amplitude Desegregation
Fader Level
key: Frequency Masking

questions.stem: This effect uses all pass filters to sweep the frequency spectrum.
options: Phaser
Flanger
Delay
Phase Scope
key: Phaser

questions.stem: This effect uses comb filtering intentionally to create a sweeping effect up and down the frequency spectrum.
options: Flanger
Phaser
Equalizer
Phase Scope
key: Flanger

questions.stem: The peaking filter is a less flexible tool for dealing with localized frequency-domain problems than a shelving filter.
options: True
False
key: False

questions.stem: One method of finding drum resonances is to boost heavily with your widest possible peaking filter, and then hunt for the offending frequency by sweeping the filter around.
options: True
False
key: False

questions.stem: A parametric EQ requires control over three parameters, namely: Frequency, Gain, and Q
options: True
False
key: True

questions.stem: A semi-parametric EQ has control over all the same parameters as a parametric EQ except frequency selection.
options: True
False
key: False

questions.stem: If you're happy with the way your dynamics processors are responding, then EQ after them; if you aren't, then try EQ'ing earlier in the chain to see if you can improve things.
options: True
False
key: True

questions.stem: A guitar sounds muddy and boosting its presence does not fix it. What is the more likely correct move?
options: Boost the presence more aggressively
Raise the fader until the presence is audible
Pan the guitar further from center
Cut the low mids that are masking the presence rather than boosting further
key: Cut the low mids that are masking the presence rather than boosting further

questions.stem: You sweep a narrow boost through a tom and find the ring that has been bothering you. What does the procedure guide have you do next?
options: Leave the boost in place and pull the track fader down to compensate
Widen the boost until it stops sounding surgical and keep it
Turn the boost into the smallest cut that solves the problem
Notch every harmonic above it at the same depth
key: Turn the boost into the smallest cut that solves the problem

questions.stem: Why does the course tell you to cut the frequency that is in the way rather than boost the one you want?
options: A cut costs no headroom, while a boost lifts the whole track and needs the fader back
Cuts are inaudible to listeners, so they cannot be judged as processing
Boosting introduces distortion in any digital equalizer
Cuts are easier to automate later in the mix
key: A cut costs no headroom, while a boost lifts the whole track and needs the fader back

questions.stem: You solo the snare, hear it as boxy, cut 500 Hz until the box is gone, and move on. Back in the full mix the snare now sounds thin. What went wrong?
options: The Q was too wide, and a narrow Q would have avoided this
Cutting always thins a track, so only boosts belong on drums
A soloed track has nothing masking it, so the problem may not exist in context
The solo buss adds its own equalization on the way to the monitors
key: A soloed track has nothing masking it, so the problem may not exist in context

questions.stem: How does the course have you choose the corner frequency for a high pass filter on a track?
options: Set it at 80 Hz on everything except the kick and the bass
Set it just below the lowest note the part actually plays
Leave it off unless the meter shows rumble on the track
Sweep it up until the track thins, then back it off until it is full again
key: Sweep it up until the track thins, then back it off until it is full again

questions.stem: A vocal needs a gentle lift of everything above 10 kHz to open up the top. Which shape does the module point you to, and why not a bell?
options: A narrow bell, because narrow is the most precise way to add top end
A high shelf, because it lifts the whole region where a bell favors one band
A high pass filter, because it clears the way for the top to come through
A wide bell, because shelving filters can only cut and not boost
key: A high shelf, because it lifts the whole region where a bell favors one band

questions.stem: A student adds bite to a guitar with a boost at 3 kHz using a Q of 8. It works on the chorus and whistles on everything else. What is the rule the module states?
options: Keep the narrow Q but cut the gain of the boost in half
Keep the narrow Q and automate it section by section
Move the boost to 5 kHz, where a narrow Q is safe to use
Use a wide Q for tonal moves and save narrow Q for resonances
key: Use a wide Q for tonal moves and save narrow Q for resonances

questions.stem: Select every move that the course would call corrective equalization rather than tonal shaping.
options: Notching a resonant ring out of a floor tom
High passing rumble out of a vocal microphone track
Adding warmth to a thin sounding acoustic guitar
Smoothing the brightness of a mix for a more polished sound
key: Notching a resonant ring out of a floor tom
High passing rumble out of a vocal microphone track

questions.stem: Select every situation where the course says something other than equalization gives the better result.
options: The microphone choice or placement was wrong for the part
The fader balance has never been set past the rough mix
The room is adding a reflection problem to the recording
The track has a resonant ring at 240 Hz that nothing else covers
key: The microphone choice or placement was wrong for the part
The fader balance has never been set past the rough mix
The room is adding a reflection problem to the recording

questions.stem: The piano and the rhythm guitar both fill 200 Hz to 800 Hz, and neither one is clear. Which approach does the course describe for making them fit?
options: Cut the range on one of them so the other has room in it
Boost the range on both so each is easier to pick out
Pan them both to the same side so they mask only each other
Raise the piano fader until it wins the range outright
key: Cut the range on one of them so the other has room in it

questions.stem: With your EQ active the track is 2 dB louder than it is bypassed, and it also sounds better. What does the procedure guide tell you to do?
options: Keep the setting, since a better sounding track is the goal
Match the levels, judge again, and revise the setting if the improvement goes away
Raise the bypassed signal by 2 dB and keep the EQ either way
Pull the whole mix down by 2 dB and move to the next track
key: Match the levels, judge again, and revise the setting if the improvement goes away

questions.stem: In the ear training exercise a boost makes the source sound like a voice coming through a telephone. Using the anchors the lab gives you, which band moved?
options: 125 Hz
1 kHz
4 kHz
8 kHz
key: 1 kHz

questions.stem: A mix sounds boxy and closed in. Using the same anchors, which band is the first place to look?
options: 63 Hz
500 Hz
4 kHz
16 kHz
key: 500 Hz

questions.stem: On the two band exercise your average score is falling and you know you are guessing. What does the lab tell you to do about it?
options: Narrow the frequency range so there are fewer bands to confuse
Move to one third octave resolution so the bands are further apart
Drop back to pink noise, so nothing in the source hides the band that moved
Raise the gain combination so the change is louder than the music
key: Drop back to pink noise, so nothing in the source hides the band that moved

questions.stem: The module calls the high pass the most useful filter in a mix and the easiest to overuse. What does overusing it across a session sound like?
options: Every track is cleaner on its own and the mix has lost its weight
The mix gets louder and the master buss starts clipping
The top end turns harsh and the cymbals start to bite
The low end gets boomy because the filters add resonance
key: Every track is cleaner on its own and the mix has lost its weight

questions.stem: Going track by track you reach the room mics, and in context they already sound the way you want. What does the assignment tell you to do?
options: Insert an EQ set flat, so the track has one like the others
High pass them at 80 Hz as a default starting point
Add a gentle high shelf so they match the other drum tracks
Leave them alone, because an EQ with no moves on it is not a move
key: Leave them alone, because an EQ with no moves on it is not a move

wiki_content/course-orientation-course-s.text:
Course Orientation: Course Schedule, Week by Week
[IMAGE: Two week diagram, module opens Monday of week one and is due Friday of week two]
Figure 1. Every module opens on a Monday and is due at 9:00 a.m. Mountain on the Friday of the following week. That gives you eleven days, not five. Nothing in this course is due at midnight.
 This course runs the whole arc of a mix twice. In the first six weeks you take a song from raw tracks to a finished stereo bounce, using only a handful of tools, so that by late September you have a complete mix of your own to listen to. Everything after that is the second pass, where each stage comes back at depth and every technique attaches to a problem you have already heard in your own work. 
 Why it is built this way.
 Most mixing courses hand back one mix at the end of the semester, so you never hear yourself improve. Here you finish a mix in week 5 and remix the same material by week 13. In week 15 you play them back to back. That comparison is the clearest evidence of what you learned, and it is yours to keep. 
 Weeks are the sequence, topics are the plan.
 Breaks and the final exam period are set by the university calendar. Every due date lives on the assignment in Canvas, which is the authority. The topic order may shift by a week if a session runs long or the studio schedule moves, and anything that changes will be announced in Canvas.

 The pivot. Everything after this is the second pass, at depth.

 Finals week.
 The two weeks to put in your calendar now
 Week 5. Your first complete mix is due. It is not meant to be polished. It is meant to be finished. 
 Week 16, finals week. The final exam is given at the scheduled final exam time for this section, not at your convenience during finals week. Look that time up now and plan travel and work around it.

wiki_content/pro-tools-fundamentals-lab-.title: Pro Tools Fundamentals: Lab 01 Manual Procedure Guide
wiki_content/pro-tools-fundamentals-lab-.text:
Pro Tools Fundamentals: Lab 01 Manual Procedure Guide
[IMAGE: Required] 
Follow this in order. Each step assumes the one before it is complete. If a step will not work, the cause is almost always something skipped earlier, not the step you are on. 
Use this guide to practice the workflow before starting the timed assignment. It explains the Pro Tools operations required by the assignment; the assignment page remains the source for the required track names, file name, timing, and submission. 
1. Build the session before importing
Create a local BWF session at 48 kHz and 24-bit with a stereo mix path, then save it to the required location using the DAPR naming convention. 
Create the required mono and stereo audio tracks. Name them before importing so each audio file has a clear destination. 
Set the main counter and ruler display to Bars and Beats. Use Samples as the time scale when making sample-accurate selections for tempo mapping. 
2. Import and place audio
Choose File > Import > Audio, locate the provided lab files, and add them to the Clip List. Choose the option that copies them into the session Audio Files folder. 
Audition unfamiliar clips from the Clip List when needed. Expand stereo files if you need to place only the left or right channel on a mono track. 
Drag each clip from the Clip List to its named track at the beginning of the session. Check that mono sources are on mono tracks and stereo sources are on stereo tracks. 
3. Identify the beat and verify the tempo map
Find a clear downbeat and make a precise sample-based selection from that downbeat to a known later bar boundary. A longer accurate selection reduces rounding error. 
Select the audio with the Time Grabber, then choose Event > Identify Beat. 
In the Bar|Beat Markers dialog, enter the musical location at the beginning and end of the selection. For example, a verified one-bar selection runs from 1|1|000 to 2|1|000; a four-bar selection runs from 1|1|000 to 5|1|000. 
Confirm the correct meter, apply the result, then loop playback to make sure the Bars and Beats ruler stays aligned with the music. Correct the selection before moving on if the grid drifts. 
[IMAGE: Pro Tools Bar and Beat Markers in the Tempo ruler] 
Figure 1. Bar and Beat Markers from the Pro Tools 2026.4.1 Reference Guide. 
4. Make the required grid edit
Set the Grid value to one-quarter note and enable Grid mode. 
At the required bar boundary, use the Selector to make the cut across the required clips. 
Move the material after the cut exactly one measure to the right. Copy the required tambourine measure into the empty bar. 
Create short fades or crossfades at every edit. Zoom in and listen across each cut before continuing. 
5. Pan, automate, and bounce
Set the required pan positions in the Mix window. 
Show Volume automation on the required track. Add breakpoints at the song start and at the specified measure, then shape the fade so it begins fully down and reaches 0 dB at the required point. 
Make a timeline selection from the beginning through the required end bar. Choose File > Bounce Mix, select the required BWF, PCM, interleaved, bit-depth, sample-rate, and offline settings, and enable Import After Bounce. 
After the bounce returns to the session, listen to the imported file and verify that it starts, ends, and plays correctly. 
Manual reference: Avid Pro Tools Reference Guide 2026.4.1, the reading for this module, "Identify Beat Command," manual pages 1149-1150. The guide also covers Clip List importing, grid editing, automation, and Bounce Mix in its relevant workflow chapters. 
This page is self-contained and does not rely on links to other Canvas pages. 
[IMAGE: Tip] 
Save before and after. Save the session before you start and again when you finish, with a version number in the name. It costs two seconds and it is the only undo that survives a crash.

wiki_content/macos-p1-getting-around-you.text:
macOS: P1: Getting Around Your Mac
 Pro Tools sits on top of macOS, and macOS has its own set of keyboard modifiers, hidden folders, and system settings that change how Pro Tools behaves. This page walks you through the five pieces of Mac navigation every mixer needs: Finder modifier keys, the Function key toggle, hiding background windows, telling Sound Preferences apart from Pro Tools Preferences, and finding the Library folder where your plug-ins and background helper processes actually live. 
 Goals
 Use Finder modifier keys to select, copy, and move files with precision. 
 Set the Function key toggle so your F-keys work as Pro Tools key commands, not media controls. 
 Hide every window except your active app with a single shortcut. 
 Explain the difference between macOS Sound Preferences and the Pro Tools Playback Engine. 
 Locate your Library folder, your installed plug-ins, and your Launch Agents and Launch Daemons. 
 Finder Modifier Keys
 Every modifier key changes what a click or a drag does in Finder. Learn these five and file management stops being guesswork. 
 Click
 - selects one file and deselects everything else.
 Shift + Click
 - selects every file between your last click and this one.
 Command + Click
 - adds or removes individual files from the selection without touching the rest.
 Option + Drag
 - copies the file to the destination instead of moving it. Use this when dragging within the same drive.
 Command + Drag
 - forces a move instead of a copy. Use this when dragging between two different drives, since Finder copies across drives by default.
 [IMAGE: Note]
 Note:
 Control + Click opens the same contextual menu as a right-click. Every Mac trackpad and mouse supports this even without a right-click button configured.
 The Function Key Toggle
 Pro Tools puts key commands on F1 through F12. macOS ships with those same keys set to control volume, brightness, and media playback instead. Set the toggle below once, and your F-keys work directly in Pro Tools. 
 [IMAGE: Warning]
 Without this setting, your F-keys turn into media keys.
 Pressing F1 lowers your screen brightness instead of triggering the Pro Tools command mapped to it. To get the true F-key signal through without changing this setting, you would have to hold Fn every single time - that is not workable mid-session. 
 Open System Settings. 
 Click Keyboard in the sidebar. 
 Click Keyboard Shortcuts. 
 Select Function Keys in the left-hand list. 
 Check Use F1, F2, etc. keys as standard function keys. 
 Close System Settings. 
 [IMAGE: Keyboard Shortcuts panel with Function Keys selected and the standard function keys toggle switched on]
 The Function Keys panel with the toggle switched on. 
 [IMAGE: Tip]
 Tip:
 With this setting on, the two functions swap places. Your F-keys now send standard F1-F12 signals to Pro Tools directly. Hold Fn at the same time as an F-key to get the media function (volume, brightness, play/pause) back.
 Hide Other Windows
 A mix session fills your screen with plugin windows, browsers, and Finder windows. One shortcut clears everything except your active app. 
 Command + H
 - hides the windows of the app you are currently in.
 Command + Option + H
 - hides every other open app and leaves only your active app's windows on screen.
 [IMAGE: Note]
 Note:
 Find the same command in the menu bar under the app name's menu, listed as Hide Others.
 Sound Preferences vs. Pro Tools Preferences
 macOS Sound settings and the Pro Tools Playback Engine are two completely separate audio paths. Changing one does not change the other. 
 [IMAGE: Required]
 These two settings control different things:
 System Settings > Sound sets the device macOS uses for system alerts, notifications, and any non-Pro-Tools audio, such as a browser tab. 
 Pro Tools > Setup > Playback Engine sets the audio interface Pro Tools uses for your session. This is independent of the macOS Sound setting. 
 Set your interface in Playback Engine for every Pro Tools session. The macOS Sound output can stay on the Mac's built-in speakers for everything else - the two settings will not conflict. 
 [IMAGE: System Settings Sound pane showing a long list of output devices including several virtual Pro Tools Audio Bridge]
 The macOS Sound pane's Output list on a real production Mac - notice how many virtual devices show up here (Pro Tools Audio Bridge, Dolby Audio Bridge, and more) alongside the actual hardware. None of these are selected in Playback Engine automatically just because they appear here. 
 Library, Plug-Ins, and Launch Agents
 Your plug-ins, and the background processes that authorize them, live inside the Library folder. macOS hides this folder from you by default. 
 [IMAGE: Note]
 Reveal your user Library folder:
 In Finder, open the Go menu, hold Option, and click Library once it appears in the list. Or use Go > Go to Folder and type ~/Library. 
 /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/
 - plug-ins installed for every user account on the machine (System Library).
 ~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/
 - plug-ins installed for your user account only (User Library).
 ~/Library/LaunchAgents and /Library/LaunchAgents
 - background helper processes that start when a single user logs in. iLok, interface drivers, and plug-in license managers install these.
 /Library/LaunchDaemons
 - background processes that start at the system level, before any user logs in. These run system-wide services rather than per-user apps.
 [IMAGE: Tip]
 Tip:
 When a plug-in or interface will not authorize, check its Launch Agent or Launch Daemon first. A stalled background helper process is the most common cause.

wiki_content/macos-p1-mac-interface-and-.text:
macOS: P1: Mac Interface and Application Behavior
 Every Mac screen is built from the same handful of pieces, and every app follows the same rules for opening, closing, and switching. Once these rules click, navigating any Mac - not just this one - stops requiring guesswork. 
 The Building Blocks of the Screen
 Desktop
 - the background layer everything else sits on top of. It can hold files and folders, and shows your wallpaper.
 Menu Bar
 - the strip across the top of the screen. Its menus - File, Edit, and the rest - always belong to whichever app is currently active, and change the instant you switch apps. System status icons live on the right side.
 Apple menu
 - the Apple logo at the far left of the Menu Bar. Unlike every other menu, it never changes no matter which app is active. It holds About This Mac, System Settings, and the Sleep, Restart, and Shut Down commands.
 Dock
 - the row of app icons along the bottom or side of the screen. A small dot under an icon means that app is currently running. The Trash sits at the end of the Dock.
 Finder
 - the file-management app that is technically always running, even with no windows open. Its icon is always the leftmost one in the Dock.
 Control Center
 - a Menu Bar icon that opens quick toggles for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, display brightness, and volume without opening System Settings.
 Notification Center
 - opened from the clock in the Menu Bar or a trackpad swipe from the right edge, showing recent alerts and widgets - a separate area from Control Center.
 Trash
 - holds deleted files until it is emptied. Files sitting in the Trash still take up drive space.
 Active Application vs. Active Window
 Only one app is active, or frontmost, at any moment - its name appears bold in the Menu Bar and its menus are the ones showing. An app can have zero windows, one window, or a dozen windows open at once. Clicking a different window that belongs to the same active app changes which window is receiving your keystrokes, but does not change which app is active. Clicking a window that belongs to a different app switches which app is active entirely. 
 Closing a Window vs. Quitting an App
 Command-W closes only the frontmost window. The app itself keeps running - its Dock icon still shows the running indicator, even with no windows visible. Command-Q quits the entire app, closing every window it owns and stopping the app completely. 
 [IMAGE: Note]
 This trips up people coming from Windows.
 On a Mac, closing every open window of an app usually does not quit that app the way it would on Windows. The app keeps running in the background with zero windows open until you explicitly quit it. 
 Switching Between Apps and Windows
 Command-Tab
 - hold Command and tap Tab repeatedly to cycle through an overlay of every open app, then release to switch to the highlighted one.
 Command-` (backtick)
 - cycles between multiple open windows that belong to the single app currently active - it does nothing if that app only has one window open.
 Hiding Applications
 Command-H
 - hides every window belonging to the active app. The app keeps running with nothing visible on screen.
 Command-Option-H
 - hides every other open app except the one you are currently using, leaving only your active app's windows visible.
 [IMAGE: Required]
 Command-Option-H is one of the most useful shortcuts in this entire unit.
 In the middle of a mix, a dozen plugin windows, a browser, and a couple of Finder windows can bury your Pro Tools session. Command-Option-H clears every bit of that clutter in one keystroke, instantly, without quitting a single app - everything you hid is still running and reappears exactly as you left it the moment you switch back. 
 [IMAGE: Before Command-Option-H: Terminal, Audio MIDI Setup, and another app all visible at once alongside Safari]
 Before: Terminal, an Audio MIDI Setup dialog, and another app all cluttering the screen alongside Safari. 
 [IMAGE: After Command-Option-H: only Safari remains visible, everything else hidden]
 After: one keystroke later, only Safari remains. Everything else is still running - just hidden.

wiki_content/macos-p1-modifier-keys-and-.title: macOS: P1: Modifier Keys and Essential Shortcuts
wiki_content/macos-p1-modifier-keys-and-.text:
macOS: P1: Modifier Keys and Essential Shortcuts
[IMAGE: Dark Toolbar with Labeled Capture Buttons]
Figure 1. Dark Toolbar with Labeled Capture Buttons.
 Five keys change the meaning of everything else you press, and a small set of shortcuts built on them cover most of what a Mac user does in a normal day. Learning these once means never hunting through a menu for something a keystroke already does faster. 
 The Five Modifier Keys
 Command (⌘)
 - the primary key behind almost every menu-command shortcut - copy, paste, save, and most of what follows on this page.
 Option (⌥)
 - unlocks alternate actions - reveals hidden menu items, forces a copy instead of a move while dragging a file, and modifies several shortcuts below into a related but different command.
 Control (⌃)
 - opens the contextual right-click menu on anything - a file, a piece of text, a Dock icon.
 Shift (⇧)
 - extends a selection to a range, and combined with Command turns several shortcuts into a related variant - notably the screenshot shortcuts below.
 Fn / Globe
 - toggles between a key's special hardware function and its standard behavior. It also triggers dictation when pressed twice.
 Everyday Editing Shortcuts
 Command-C / Command-V
 - copy and paste - the most-used shortcut pair on any computer.
 Command-X
 - cut. Unlike copy, this removes the original the moment you cut it, before you have pasted anywhere - use it carefully.
 Command-Z
 - undo the last action. Pro Tools uses the identical shortcut for undoing edits inside a session.
 Command-A
 - select everything in the current window or field.
 Command-F
 - open a find or search field inside the current app.
 Command-S
 - save the current document or session.
 Command-I
 - opens Get Info in Finder, or applies italics in a text field, depending on which app is active.
 App and Window Management, Recapped
 Command-Tab, Command-` (backtick), Command-H, Command-Option-H, Command-W, and Command-Q all live on the Mac Interface and Application Behavior page - Command-Option-H in particular is worth knowing before anything else in this unit, since it clears visual clutter in a busy mix session in a single keystroke. 
 Force Quit, Directly
 Option-Command-Escape
 - opens the Force Quit Applications window immediately, skipping the Apple menu entirely. Full troubleshooting guidance for when to use this lives on the Force Quit and Troubleshooting page.
 Finder and Capture Shortcuts
 Shift-Command-G
 - opens Go to Folder, letting you type a path and jump straight there - covered in depth on the Finder Deep Dive page.
 Shift-Command-.
 - toggles whether hidden files and folders are visible in Finder.
 Shift-Command-3 / 4 / 5
 - capture the whole screen, a selected area, or open the full screenshot and recording toolbar - covered in depth on the Spotlight, Quick Look, and Screenshots page.
 Spotlight and Quick Look, Previewed
 Command-Space opens Spotlight, a system-wide search box for finding an app or file by name instead of navigating to it manually. Pressing Space with a file selected in Finder opens Quick Look, a preview of that file's contents without launching its full app. Both get a full page of their own next, including a practical example using Audio MIDI Setup. 
 [IMAGE: Tip]
 Tie every shortcut to a muscle you already use.
 If a shortcut here has an equivalent inside Pro Tools - undo, save, find - practice the macOS version until it is automatic. The two will not fight each other; they apply in different contexts, and having both wired in removes a constant, tiny mental tax during a session.

wiki_content/macos-p1-mouse-and-trackpad.text:
macOS: P1: Mouse and Trackpad Settings
 You touch your pointing device constantly through a mix session - dragging automation, zooming a waveform, right-clicking a track for the edit menu. A handful of settings in System Settings control exactly how that pointing device behaves, and getting them right removes a surprising amount of daily friction. 
 Where These Settings Live
 Open System Settings. An external mouse is configured under Mouse, and the built-in trackpad is configured under Trackpad - two separate panels, and each panel only appears in the sidebar while that hardware is actually connected. 
 Settings That Affect a Mix Session
 Tracking speed
 - how far the on-screen pointer travels per inch of physical movement. A slower speed trades raw travel distance for finer control - useful when nudging a single automation breakpoint.
 Scroll direction (Natural vs. traditional)
 - "Natural" scrolling moves on-screen content the same direction you drag your fingers, matching how a touchscreen behaves. Turning it off flips scrolling to the traditional direction older Windows and Mac systems used.
 Secondary click
 - which physical click or corner opens a contextual menu (a right-click). On a mouse this is usually the right side; on a trackpad it can be set to a specific corner or a two-finger click.
 Tap to Click (trackpad)
 - whether a light tap registers as a full click, instead of requiring the trackpad to physically depress.
 Force Click and haptic feedback (trackpad)
 - a firmer press that triggers a secondary action, such as a Quick Look preview or dictionary lookup. Pressure sensitivity and the click feel itself can both be adjusted.
 [IMAGE: Note]
 Scroll direction and Pro Tools zoom.
 Scroll direction determines which way you scroll to zoom in versus out in the Edit window. A mismatched scroll direction setting is one of the most common "my zoom feels backwards" complaints in a lab - check this setting first before assuming Pro Tools itself is misbehaving. 
 [IMAGE: System Settings Mouse pane showing Tracking speed, Natural scrolling, Secondary click, Double-Click Speed]
 The Mouse settings pane. Trackpad has its own separate pane with the same tracking and scrolling controls, plus Tap to Click and Force Click. 
 [IMAGE: Tip]
 Tip:
 If you switch between a Mac trackpad at home and a mouse in the lab, expect tracking speed to feel different between the two - each device has its own separate speed setting, so adjusting one does not change the other.
